# 3. Escalation Guidelines
A fistfight does not suddenly escalate into a gunfight. Use common sense. - Roleplaying should ALWAYS be attempted before mechanical fighting - Essentially, you MUST talk and warn the other party that you WILL shoot before doing so, giving them a chance to opt out of combat by cooperation! - NO suckerpunching or magdumping people without warning!! - The basic Hostility Escalation guidelines are as follows: -- Hail (if ship-to-ship) and attempt conversation. -- Attempt a show of force, specifically brandishing and making it known you have and will use Non-Lethal force. -- Utilize Non-Lethal force. -- Make every effort to advise you will use Lethal force. -- Utilize Lethal force. - Steps 2 and 3 can be bypassed (unless playing NFSD/Command, see special rules for that), provided you make it clear you will resort to lethal force. - Note that this is an outline of what should at least be attempted in all situations. It is understood that not every dynamic situation can follow this exactly, but leaping straight to lethals with no warning may get you bwoinked - Controlling escalation/heat is one of the most essential skills to master
Additional notes: - Antagonistic ghost roles and pest ghost roles like mice are always fair game for attack. - As a non-antagonist, don't attack Nanotrasen-aligned ghost roles like familiars, drones, or pets without provocation. - Do not attack another player without a legitimate, explainable roleplay reason that could be applied in a similar, real-life scenario. - Cap metagrudges (IC grudges) at grumbling annoyance and snarky comments. Dont escalate to violence over grievances from previous rounds. - If a fight results in someone being critically injured or killed, seek medical help for them. - If a fight ends and both parties leave the area, you cannot skip escalation and plunge back into a fight. What's done is done. - A 15 minute non-aggression period is required after respawning, so you can't immediately get in a ship and try to go kill whoever killed you. - NFSD and command roles must resolve situations with non-lethal force and de-escalate IC confrontation except in cases where there is a reasonable chance of harm/death.
